summary: The agent implemented most of the feature: all baseline tests passed and 133 of 137 new tests passed, but four explicit integrity edge cases remain incorrect.

details.reasoning: The failures are in the modified TextFileBasedViolationStore implementation. It rejects a shared entry before checking whether another entry owns the same out-of-folder path, identifies unowned files only by recorded spelling rather than by the file reached through a link, discards the resolved identity of broken/out-of-folder entries so they cannot be shared, and does not catch InvalidPathException while analyzing an index entry. These omissions directly cause the four failing tests.
details.secondary_factors: The trajectory records optional Spotless/SpotBugs checks being blocked by Maven Central timeouts, but compilation and the visible baseline tests completed; this did not cause the graded failures.

quick_failure_summary: Four integrity edge cases fail: shared unsafe paths, symlink ownership, shared outside paths, and malformed recorded names.

justification.issue_description: Integrity analysis and repair do not preserve file identity and ownership information for unsafe or malformed recorded paths, and save-time forgetting checks safety before sharing.
justification.evidence: The prompt explicitly says that two entries whose recorded names resolve to one file are shared, that an entry both shared and another condition stays shared, that a regular file reached by an entry is not unowned, that every entry in any condition is reported, and that forgetting deletes a file unless another entry shares it. The implementation instead checks unsafe status before sharing in forgetResolvedRule, considers only regular resolutions in byResolvedFile, uses recordedNames alone in findUnownedFiles, and calls Path.resolve without catching InvalidPathException.
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is a missed requirement rather than a verifier mismatch: the hidden tests exercise combinations expressly described by the task, and their failures are deterministic application-level failures. The implementation is substantial and otherwise passes the baseline and 133 new tests, but these requirements were not completed.

problem_assessment.notes: The task is difficult but solvable and the reference implementation confirms feasibility. The new tests comprehensively exercise the stated path, link, sharing, repair, ordering, and concurrency rules; the four failures correspond to documented or directly implied behavior rather than undocumented conventions.

evidence: junit_base.xml reports 42 tests with 0 failures and 0 errors; junit_new.xml reports 137 tests with 4 failures and 0 errors.
All four new-test failures are application exceptions or assertions whose stacks point into TextFileBasedViolationStore.forgetResolvedRule, analyze, or resolve, after normal test setup completed.
test_execution.log reports wrapper exit code 1 with baseline_passed=True (42/42) and new_tests_passed=False (133/137), so the verifier ran normally.

trajectory.json shows the agent changed only the production store file and completed compilation and visible test checks; it also records optional formatter/SpotBugs checks affected by Maven Central timeouts, but those checks were not the graded test path.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external environment or verifier blocker explains the failures; the optional dependency timeouts reduced only ancillary validation and did not prevent the agent from completing or running its available tests.
